title: Getting ready for pregnancy
quick_answer: You do not need a perfect three-year plan. Start with ordinary health care and a few proven steps.
learn_more: Review health history, medications, dental care and vaccination needs with a clinician. Both partners can reduce smoke and workplace exposure. Earlier planning can be useful for conditions that need time to manage, but there is no established ideal three-year routine.
visible_safety: No fixed preparation deadline or fertility guarantee. Never stop prescribed medicine on your own.

title: Folic acid before conception
quick_answer: Folic acid helps prevent serious problems in a baby's developing brain and spine.
learn_more: US guidance supports folic acid before pregnancy and in early pregnancy. Food folate matters too, but a supplement's total folate label is not the same as its folic acid amount. Common MTHFR variants do not remove the evidence for folic acid.
visible_safety: Higher-risk dosing belongs with a clinician; no methylfolate substitution claim or automatic dose.

quick_answer: Serious problems can happen during pregnancy and after birth. Get medical care immediately for warning signs.

visible_safety: Call 911 in the US for life-threatening symptoms or imminent danger. Do not wait for a checklist or routine visit.

title: Milestones and screening
quick_answer: Use milestones to notice skills, not grade your child.
learn_more: US developmental screening recommendations include nine, eighteen and thirty months, and autism screening at eighteen and twenty-four months. Concerns may prompt earlier assessment. Corrected age can help interpret preterm developmental progress.
visible_safety: No diagnosis or reassurance solely from milestone cards; loss of skills or concerns need evaluation.

title: Screens and family languages
quick_answer: Children benefit from people, play and conversation in their family's languages.
learn_more: Screen studies are largely observational; background TV and some viewing contexts correlate with less favorable outcomes. Co-viewing differs from solitary viewing. Multilingual exposure does not itself cause a language disorder.
visible_safety: Use age-appropriate guidance; no screen-based IQ prediction or guilt.

title: Starting complementary foods
quick_answer: Around six months, babies may be ready to add suitable foods while continuing milk feeds.
learn_more: Readiness, texture and swallowing ability matter. Breast milk or formula remains central through the first year. Offer varied iron-containing foods and safe textures; neither spoon-feeding nor baby-led approaches guarantee better outcomes.
visible_safety: No solids before four months, no cereal in bottle, no honey under twelve months; swallowing concerns require individual guidance.

title: Allergens and choking prevention
quick_answer: Safe food introduction and allergy planning matter more than rushing.
learn_more: Peanut prevention research supports appropriate early introduction in eligible infants; those with severe eczema or egg allergy need a clinician-guided plan. Food shape and texture affect choking risk; supervise eating upright.
visible_safety: Never give whole nuts or choking hazards; severe allergic reaction or choking is an emergency; follow written action plan.

learn_more: Growth charts track patterns, not a grade or body goal. Children eat different amounts from day to day. Caregivers provide appropriate food opportunities; children are not required to finish a plate.
visible_safety: No calorie restriction, automated growth diagnosis, forced feeding or target weight.

quick_answer: Simple safety habits matter throughout childhood.

visible_safety: No equipment guarantee; drowning, poisoning or choking requires emergency action.

quick_answer: Keep a pediatric care plan and discuss current immunization recommendations.

title: Toddler toilet learning
quick_answer: Toilet learning should be gentle and responsive, not a race.
learn_more: Assisted toileting and independent continence are distinct. Earlier initiation may not mean earlier autonomous skills. Evidence does not establish that a specific diaper company or product causes delayed training.
visible_safety: No punishment, forced sitting, fluid restriction or withholding; pain or constipation concerns need care.

title: Natural infant remedies and experimental practices
quick_answer: Natural does not mean safe for an infant.
learn_more: Probiotics have strain-specific evidence and serious risks in preterm infants. Vaginal seeding is research-only; placenta capsules have an infection concern. Essential oils, honey under twelve months and unsafe teething products can harm babies.
visible_safety: No home vaginal seeding, placenta encapsulation, infant spinal manipulation, essential oil ingestion, preterm probiotic or honey under twelve months.
